questions.question: Explain what is meant by describing a machine as a system, trace the chain of mechanisms in a bicycle, and describe the block diagram that represents it.
questions.expected_answer: A system has an input, the force or movement supplied, a process, what the mechanism does to it by changing size, direction, speed or type of movement, and an output, the force or movement delivered where the work is done. In a bicycle the foot pushes a pedal, which is a lever on a crank that turns the chainwheel; the chain carries the rotation to a smaller sprocket on the back wheel so it turns faster; the wheel and axle makes the rim move faster still with less force; and the tyre pushes on the road to move the bicycle. The output of each mechanism is the input of the next. A block diagram shows this as a box for input, an arrow, a box for each mechanism in order, an arrow and a box for output.

questions.question: Define mechanical advantage, explain the trade it always involves, and show how the advantages of mechanisms in a chain combine, with an example and the crane's own chain.
questions.expected_answer: Mechanical advantage is load divided by effort, the number of times a mechanism multiplies the input force; the price is distance, since the effort moves further than the load by the same factor and no mechanism gives something for nothing. In a chain the advantages multiply: a lever of two feeding a pulley system of three gives six, and the hand moves six times as far as the load. A car jack combines a crank and a screw to lift a car with a hand force. Mechanisms can also trade force for speed, as the egg beater's gears do. In the crane the hand turns a crank that winds a drum, giving the force advantage, and the string passes over a single pulley at the arm's tip that gives no force advantage but changes the pull from horizontal to vertical.

questions.question: Describe how to analyse an unfamiliar machine, using the fishing reel or hand drill as an example, and list the signatures by which the five simple mechanisms are recognised.
questions.expected_answer: Ask what goes in, what each part does and what comes out. In a fishing reel the hand turns a crank, a gear pair turns the spool several times per handle turn, and the spool as a wheel and axle winds the line in fast, a speed advantage paid for with effort. In a hand drill the crank turns a large bevel gear that drives a small one at right angles so the bit spins fast with less force. The signatures: a lever is a rigid bar turning about a pivot; a wheel and axle is two different-sized circles turning on one centre; a pulley is a grooved wheel with a rope; a gear is a toothed wheel meshing with another; and an inclined plane, wedge or screw is a slope that is straight, pointed or wrapped round a rod. A single fixed pulley changes direction only and does not multiply force.
